extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for Stanford researchers on preparing and submitting an Invention Disclosure to the Office of Technology Licensing (OTL), including what to include, timing to preserve patent rights, and how OTL will process and preliminarily evaluate the disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible submitters
rubrics_metrics.description: Stanford faculty, staff and students can submit an Invention Disclosure through the Researcher Portal on the Office of Technology Licensing (OTL) website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended audience is Stanford-affiliated researchers; use OTL resources for campus-specific policies and contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission channel
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit an Invention Disclosure through the Researcher Portal on the OTL website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the official 'Submit an Invention Disclosure to OTL' link/portal; do not rely on informal emails for formal disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content completeness (describe new aspects)
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure should fully describe the new aspects of the invention, including the critical solution it provides and its advantages and benefits over current technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a thorough description of what is new and different, the technical solution, and clear statements of advantages/benefits compared to existing technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing to preserve patent rights (avoid public disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: To preserve patent rights, inventors should disclose inventions before publications (e.g., conference abstracts, manuscripts, etc.) or presentations describing the invention are publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not present, publish, or otherwise publicly disclose the invention prior to filing/working with OTL; examples called out include conference abstracts and manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: OTL logging and docketing
rubrics_metrics.description: OTL logs in all disclosures it receives, assigns a docket number, and assigns each one to a specific licensing manager who is responsible for all actions relating to the docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After submission expect an official docket number and assignment of a licensing manager who will track the matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: OTL follow-up and inventor meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Shortly after the Invention Disclosure is submitted, an OTL licensing manager will contact the inventor(s) to discuss the invention and its commercial potential and will meet with the inventor(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to meet with the licensing manager and discuss technical details, potential applications, timelines, and any supporting data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary evaluation — novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: An OTL licensing manager will make a preliminary evaluation of novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be ready to explain how the invention differs from prior art and existing solutions; provide references or known prior work if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary evaluation — potential commercial applications
rubrics_metrics.description: OTL will evaluate potential commercial applications of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe possible uses, adoption scenarios, and why the invention would be valuable to potential licensees or users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary evaluation — possible markets
rubrics_metrics.description: OTL will evaluate possible markets for the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide information on target customers, market size or segments, and competitive landscape where possible to support market assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy and resources reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant Stanford resources and policies are linked (e.g., Chapter 9 Intellectual Property, OTL For Researchers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Chapter 9 IP and OTL resources for detailed policy, procedures, and contacts (e.g., OTL executive director contact provided).
